response: Yes, income-related differences in active travel are associated with physical environmental characteristics. Studies have shown that individuals from lower-income backgrounds are more likely to live in areas with poorer physical environmental characteristics, such as limited access to safe and walkable roads, sidewalks, and bike lanes, which can discourage active travel. In contrast, higher-income areas often have more favorable physical environments that support walking and cycling, such as well-maintained sidewalks, bike paths, and aesthetic features like parks and green spaces. These physical environmental characteristics can contribute to income-related differences in active travel, with lower-income individuals facing more barriers to engaging in physical activity through walking or cycling.
